title: The Most Important Thing
subtitle: Uncommon Sense for the Thoughtful Investor
author: Howard Marks
qualificationRationale: Co-founder of Oaktree Capital ($180B+ AUM); Warren Buffett famously reads Marks' memos the moment they arrive for second-level thinking and market cycle analysis.

title: Shoe Dog
subtitle: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
author: Phil Knight
qualificationRationale: Candid memoir revered by founders for detailing the chaotic realities of supply chains, cash crunches, and relentless survival in physical commerce.

title: Deep Work
subtitle: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World
author: Cal Newport
qualificationRationale: Crystallized the cognitive value of uninterrupted concentration in the knowledge economy; cited across academia and technology sectors.

title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
subtitle: A Guide to Wealth and Happiness
author: Eric Jorgenson
qualificationRationale: Distills permissionless leverage, specific knowledge, and judgment from AngelList's founder; acclaimed across modern technology and venture capital.

title: The Innovator's Dilemma
subtitle: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail
author: Clayton M. Christensen
qualificationRationale: Introduced the theory of disruptive innovation; cited as the only business book Steve Jobs publicly endorsed and embraced to reshape Apple.

title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits
subtitle: And Other Writings
author: Philip A. Fisher
qualificationRationale: Pioneer of growth investing and the 'scuttlebutt' method; directly molded Warren Buffett's transition from pure value to quality-growth businesses.

title: Four Thousand Weeks
subtitle: Time Management for Mortals
author: Oliver Burkeman
qualificationRationale: Subversive philosophical critique of productivity culture; praised by cognitive psychologists for anchoring personal time management in existential finitude.
